quiz_title: 📱 تطبيقات الموبايل للصغار - MIT Mobile App - Challenge 1

questions.question: What is the primary web-based platform we use to build Android mobile applications without coding?
questions.explanation: Spot on! MIT App Inventor is our drag-and-drop tool to construct real mobile apps.

questions.question: Which view in MIT App Inventor is used to select and design how your app looks (adding buttons, textboxes, and labels)?
questions.explanation: Correct! Designer View is where we place buttons, labels, images, and arrange the look of our user interface.

questions.question: Which view is used to program the actions and logic of your application using drag-and-drop puzzle blocks?
questions.explanation: Excellent! Blocks View is where we script the application logic, variables, and math operators.

questions.question: What component should you drag in if you want to display static descriptive titles or text outputs on the screen?
questions.explanation: Great! A Label is designed specifically for displaying static or updated text, unlike a button that clicks or a textbox that takes inputs.

questions.question: Which non-visible component allows your phone to read words out loud to the player?
questions.explanation: Perfect! The TextToSpeech component converts typed text strings into virtual spoken audio outputs.

questions.question: What block trigger is fired immediately when a user taps or touches a button component on the phone screen?
questions.explanation: Spot on! The 'when Button.Click' event block is the standard block to run scripts when a button is tapped.

questions.question: How can you test and run your MIT App Inventor app live on a real physical Android phone?
options: Using the AI Companion mobile app
You cannot run it on real phones
questions.explanation: Excellent! Using the MIT AI Companion app lets you scan QR codes to test your running app live!

questions.question: Under which drawer in the Designer Palette can you find buttons, labels, and textboxes?
questions.explanation: Correct! The User Interface drawer houses standard user widgets like buttons, textboxes, checkboxes, and labels.

questions.question: Is the TextToSpeech component visible on the actual phone screen during gameplay?
options: Yes, it looks like a mouth
No, it is a non-visible component that runs in the background
Yes, it displays text on the screen
Only when the phone is shaking
questions.explanation: Great! Non-visible components (like sensors and voices) do not display widgets on the interface but provide great tools in the background.

questions.question: In which drawer in the Blocks panel can you find logic blocks (like true/false or equals)?
questions.explanation: Perfect! The Logic drawer contains comparison blocks, true, false, and logical and/or/not operators.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to make the TextToSpeech1 voice say 'Hello Developer' when Button1 is clicked.
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Attaching the Speak block inside the Button.Click event script activates the text reader immediately upon clicking!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to get the text entered by the player from TextBox1 and speak it using TextToSpeech1.
questions.explanation: Perfect! Passing the TextBox1.Text property into the speak function dynamically vocalizes any text strings input by the user.
